Since neither the pip binary route nor the from-source build route is feasible without network access or pre-installed toolchains, envpool could not be installed into the active Python environment.

finish_summary: Attempted to install envpool from the local checkout but could not produce a working installation. EnvPool's native C++ extensions are built via Bazel (see Makefile targets bazel-build/bazel-release which invoke `bazel run //:setup -- bdist_wheel`), but no Bazel/Bazelisk binary or Go toolchain is present anywhere on the system, and the sandbox has no network access (pip is configured with --no-index and only a local /wheels dir containing basic build tooling like setuptools/numpy/cython, none of which include Bazel, dm-env, gymnasium, or envpool-assets). I tried `pip install -e .` which failed immediately on missing `dm-env` (a runtime dependency, unavailable offline). Forcing `--no-deps` allowed `setup.py develop` to complete only because it does not invoke the Bazel build step in a plain (non-bazel-run) `pip install` — it merely registers the pure-Python package metadata with no compiled `_envpool.so` extension modules present anywhere in the tree.
